style.color_palette: Warm ivory drafting-paper background, deep navy typography, faint square grid, cobalt blue for AEM structure and traces, green for verified runtime behavior, violet for authored layout state, and restrained orange for configuration drift or unsafe overrides.

deck_context.source_summary: Class 14 of a seven-week traditional AEM Sites course, delivered Thursday, September 3, 2026. The audience already understands editable templates, policies, HTL, client libraries, Core Components, proxies and responsive image delivery. This class connects those foundations to AEM Layout Container, responsive grid, breakpoints, Layout Mode, persisted layout evidence and component behavior inside authored columns.
deck_context.core_claim: A responsive AEM page is a traceable contract: templates enable the grid, authors create breakpoint-specific composition in Layout Mode, AEM persists and renders grid decisions, project CSS cooperates with the assigned columns, and the browser proves layout and media delivery.
canonical_facts: The Layout Container provides a grid paragraph system that can be used as the page's main content container, an authorable component, or both.
The Core Container Component uses layout = responsiveGrid when it owns AEM responsive layout behavior.
Layout Mode lets authors resize and position components with horizontal snap-to-grid behavior for configured breakpoints.
The emulator and breakpoint configuration support authoring, while rendered CSS and the browser remain the runtime authority.
Project responsive-grid CSS boundaries must agree with the breakpoints configured for the page editor.
AEM responsive layout state is persisted for component resources and becomes browser-visible aem-Grid and aem-GridColumn classes.
Grid columns own the component's available page width; component CSS owns behavior inside that assigned space.
Project CSS should not globally override AEM grid classes to repair one component.
Core Image policy widths define available candidates; browser-native responsive markup lets the browser choose a source.
Rendered image dimensions and transferred bytes are separate evidence.
Local image evidence can use the Adaptive Image Servlet; Web-Optimized Image Delivery is an AEM as a Cloud Service capability.
Adobe recommends keeping nested responsive grids as flat as practical.
